classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that expansion and double-angle reduction must precede auxiliary-angle conversion, retaining a constant offset and doubled argument.

content.prompt: Convert $f(x)=\cos x(\sin x+\cos x)$ to an appropriate auxiliary-angle form.

answer.short:
$f(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt2}\sin\left(2x+\frac\pi4\right)$.

Use double-angle identities before matching coefficients.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\sin x\cos x+\cos^2x\\f(x)&=\frac12\sin2x+\frac12(1+\cos2x)\\f(x)&=\frac12+\frac12\sin2x+\frac12\cos2x.\end{align*}$$
For $R\sin(2x+\alpha)$, equating coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=\frac12$ and $R\sin\alpha=\frac12$. Hence $R=\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and $\alpha=\frac\pi4$.
$$f(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt2}\sin\left(2x+\frac\pi4\right).$$
